title: Cabin Safety Risk Assessment
description: Free Cabin Safety Risk Assessment template for aviation you can edit online and download as PDF. Covers cabin operations information, cabin safety risk assessment matrix, cabin crew duties and responsibilities.

Turbulence Management Procedures

TURBULENCE SEVERITY:

☐ LIGHT: Slight erratic changes. Passengers feel slight strain against seatbelts.

☐ MODERATE: Changes in altitude/attitude. Aircraft remains in control. Passengers feel definite strain.

☐ SEVERE: Abrupt changes. Aircraft may be out of control momentarily. Passengers forced against belts.

☐ EXTREME: Aircraft violently tossed, impossible to control. May cause structural damage.

TURBULENCE ACTION PROCEDURES:

FORECAST/ENCOUNTEREDCREW ACTION
Light Turbulence Forecast-Continue service with caution
-Secure loose items
-PA announcement to return to seats
Moderate Turbulence Forecast-Suspend service
-Secure all carts and equipment
-PA announcement to return to seats and fasten belts
-Crew to take assigned seats
Severe Turbulence Encountered-Immediate PA to return to seats and fasten belts
-Abandon service immediately
-Crew to take nearest seat and fasten
-Brace position if required

TURBULENCE INJURY PREVENTION:

☐ Monitor seatbelt sign usage ☐ Regular PA announcements

☐ Anticipate turbulent areas ☐ Secure cabin before turbulence

☐ Stow service carts properly ☐ Crew jumpseat discipline

☐ Report turbulence to flight deck ☐ Complete turbulence reports

Fire And Smoke Procedures

FIRE/SMOKE DETECTION:

☐ Visual observation ☐ Smell ☐ Passenger report ☐ Smoke detection system

FIRE FIGHTING PROCEDURE - P.A.S.S.:

P - PULL the pin

A - AIM at the base of the fire

S - SQUEEZE the handle

S - SWEEP from side to side

FIRE FIGHTING CREW COMMUNICATION - C.L.O.U.D.:

C - Communicate type and location

L - Locate the fire

O - Obtain appropriate extinguisher

U - Unaffected crew member to communicate with flight deck

D - Determine best attack method

SMOKE REMOVAL PROCEDURES:

1. Don PBE/smoke hood

2. Identify source of smoke

3. Coordinate with flight deck for smoke removal

4. Use appropriate extinguisher

5. Monitor for re-ignition

6. Prepare for possible diversion

FIRE TYPES:

☐ CLASS A: Wood, paper, fabric - Use water or dry chemical

☐ CLASS B: Flammable liquids - Use Halon or CO2

☐ CLASS C: Electrical - Use Halon or CO2

☐ CLASS D: Combustible metals - Specialized agents only

☐ CLASS K: Cooking oils - Use wet chemical

Unruly Passenger Management

LEVELS OF DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOR:

LEVEL 1 - Mild: Verbally disruptive, non-compliance with crew instructions

LEVEL 2 - Moderate: Physical actions, verbal threats, sexual harassment

LEVEL 3 - Severe: Physical assault, life-threatening behavior, attempted breach of cockpit

DE-ESCALATION TECHNIQUES:

☐ Stay calm and professional ☐ Use non-threatening body language

☐ Listen actively ☐ Empathize where appropriate

☐ Set clear boundaries ☐ Offer choices where possible

☐ Avoid confrontation ☐ Use calming tone of voice

RESTRAINT PROCEDURES:

☐ Only as last resort ☐ Minimum force necessary

☐ Use approved restraint devices ☐ Monitor passenger condition

☐ Document all actions ☐ Witnesses present

REPORTING:

☐ Inform captain immediately ☐ Complete unruly passenger report

☐ Provide statement to authorities ☐ Support prosecution if required
